page: Amazon Web Services m5a.large is a general-purpose virtual server built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at 2.5 GHz, configured with 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with multithreading enabled. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It includes no local storage and has a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the performance of this instance in the lower tiers. The single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests yield scores of 581.69, which fall into the bottom 10% of tested hardware. Similarly, the Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores are 722.0 and 956.0 respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 77.28 GB/sec and a write large block speed of 13.58 GB/sec, both ranking in the bottom 10%. Static web serving throughput is measured at 1.55 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations reach 1.22 million operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of the m5a.large is its lower computational and memory throughput compared to newer hardware generations. However, because it utilizes dedicated CPU allocation on an older AMD EPYC platform, it offers a cost-efficient option for workloads that require a stable general-purpose environment without high-performance demands. Lacking local storage and GPU acceleration, this instance is best suited for lightweight applications, basic web serving, small-scale development environments, and low-throughput background utility tasks.
